anchors: Record a `rejected` entry for each upstream part Step 3 deliberately left out
decision: Before the adoption commit, record the adoption's decisions in the new skill's ledger with skill_decisions.py add --from-file: a rejected entry for each upstream part deliberately left out, and an anchored rule entry for each house rule added that upstream does not have; the ledger and the checklist naming the ids go in the adoption commit.

evidence.text: Plan M3.5 (2026-11-06). Probes: two opus arms on the pre-edit text named no durable record of a removed upstream section beyond the commit message; with the new text two opus and one haiku arm wrote both entries and ran add, and a control adoption that decided nothing wrote none.

reopen_if: Re-syncing an adopted skill gains its own mechanism that records and enforces the local delta against upstream, or the per-skill ledger is retired.
why: A commit message guards nothing: a later sync from upstream would re-import a removed part and drop an added rule silently. The ledger is what the next editor of the skill is shown (meta-skill-writer Step 0b), and the commit gate refuses a change that drops a live rule anchor.
